Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 1) The most common cause of a solitary thyroid nodule is:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Most solitary thyroid nodules are benign. Colloid nodules are far more common than malignant lesions.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 2) The commonest malignant tumor of the thyroid is:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Papillary carcinoma accounts for about 80% of thyroid cancers. It has an excellent prognosis and spreads mainly via lymphatics.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 3) The investigation of choice for evaluating a thyroid nodule is:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: FNAC is the first-line investigation for thyroid nodules. It reliably differentiates benign from most malignant lesions.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 4) The commonest route of spread of papillary thyroid carcinoma is:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Papillary carcinoma commonly metastasizes to cervical lymph nodes. Distant spread is uncommon.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 5) Follicular carcinoma most commonly spreads through:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Follicular carcinoma characteristically spreads hematogenously, especially to bone and lungs.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 6) The most common cause of hyperthyroidism is:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Graves’ disease is an autoimmune disorder and the leading cause of hyperthyroidism in adults.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 7) Which thyroid carcinoma is associated with RET proto-oncogene mutation?
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Medullary thyroid carcinoma arises from parafollicular (C) cells and is associated with RET mutations and MEN 2 syndromes.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 8) Medullary carcinoma arises from:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: C cells secrete calcitonin, which serves as an important tumor marker in medullary carcinoma.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 9) Which tumor marker is elevated in medullary thyroid carcinoma?
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Serum calcitonin is the most useful biochemical marker for diagnosis and follow-up of medullary thyroid carcinoma.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 10) The most aggressive thyroid malignancy is:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Anaplastic carcinoma is rapidly progressive with a very poor prognosis and is usually unresectable at presentation.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 11) The first investigation in a patient with diffuse thyroid swelling is:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Thyroid function tests determine whether the gland is hypo-, hyper- or euthyroid and guide further evaluation.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 12) The investigation of choice for assessing thyroid morphology is:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Ultrasound accurately evaluates thyroid size, nodules, cystic changes and cervical lymph nodes.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 13) Which thyroid carcinoma has the best prognosis?
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Papillary carcinoma has an excellent long-term survival, especially in younger patients with localized disease.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 14) A “cold” nodule on thyroid scan is:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Most cold nodules are benign, but they carry a higher risk of malignancy than hot nodules and require cytological evaluation.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 15) Which thyroid nodule has the lowest risk of malignancy?
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Autonomously functioning (“hot”) nodules are rarely malignant and usually present with hyperthyroidism.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: ১৬) The nerve most commonly injured during thyroidectomy is:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: external laryngeal nerve  laryngeal nerve injury causes hoarseness of voice. Careful identification during surgery reduces this complication.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 17) Bilateral recurrent laryngeal nerve injury causes:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Bilateral vocal cord paralysis may cause severe respiratory distress and requires urgent airway management.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 18) The most common cause of hypocalcaemia after thyroidectomy is:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.option2: Accidental removal or devascularization of parathyroid glands
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Transient hypoparathyroidism is a recognized complication of thyroid surgery and presents with hypocalcaemia.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 19) Chvostek’s and Trousseau’s signs indicate:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: These are classic clinical signs of neuromuscular irritability caused by low serum calcium.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 20) The most feared postoperative complication following thyroidectomy is:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: A rapidly expanding neck hematoma can compress the airway and is a surgical emergency requiring immediate wound decompression.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 21) Which of the following is an indication for surgery in multinodular goitre?
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Compressive symptoms such as dysphagia, dyspnea or stridor are absolute indications for thyroidectomy.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 22) A thyroid swelling that moves with protrusion of the tongue is most likely:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: A thyroglossal cyst moves with both swallowing and tongue protrusion due to its attachment to the hyoid bone.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 23) The treatment of choice for a thyroglossal duct cyst is:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: The Sistrunk procedure removes the cyst, tract and central portion of the hyoid bone, minimizing recurrence.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 24) Which thyroid carcinoma is most commonly associated with prior neck irradiation?
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Previous childhood radiation exposure is a well-known risk factor for papillary thyroid carcinoma.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 25) The most common presentation of papillary thyroid carcinoma is:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Most patients present with a painless solitary thyroid nodule. Cervical lymphadenopathy may also be present.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 26) Which thyroid carcinoma commonly shows psammoma bodies?
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Psammoma bodies and “Orphan Annie eye” nuclei are characteristic microscopic features of papillary carcinoma.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 27) Which investigation cannot differentiate follicular adenoma from follicular carcinoma?
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Diagnosis requires demonstration of capsular or vascular invasion, which FNAC cannot assess.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 28) The diagnosis of follicular carcinoma depends on:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Histological evidence of capsular or vascular invasion distinguishes follicular carcinoma from follicular adenoma.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 29) Which thyroid malignancy commonly produces amyloid in the stroma?
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Amyloid deposition derived from calcitonin is a characteristic histological feature of medullary carcinoma.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 30) Which syndrome is associated with medullary thyroid carcinoma?
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Medullary thyroid carcinoma is associated with MEN 2A and MEN 2B due to RET proto-oncogene mutations.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 31) Which thyroid carcinoma is not treated with radioactive iodine?
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Medullary carcinoma arises from C cells, which do not take up iodine; therefore radioactive iodine is ineffective.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 32) Serum thyroglobulin is most useful in the follow-up of:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: After total thyroidectomy, rising thyroglobulin suggests recurrent or residual differentiated thyroid cancer.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 33) Which thyroid carcinoma has the poorest prognosis?
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Anaplastic carcinoma is highly aggressive, rapidly invasive and associated with very low survival.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 34) The most common cause of hypothyroidism worldwide is:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Globally, iodine deficiency remains the leading cause of hypothyroidism, although Hashimoto thyroiditis predominates in iodine-sufficient regions.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 35) The most common cause of hypothyroidism in iodine-sufficient countries is:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Hashimoto thyroiditis is an autoimmune disorder causing gradual destruction of thyroid tissue.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 36) Which antibody is most commonly positive in Hashimoto thyroiditis?
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Anti-thyroid peroxidase antibodies are present in most patients with Hashimoto thyroiditis.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 37) Which thyroid disorder is associated with exophthalmos?
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Graves’ ophthalmopathy is caused by autoimmune inflammation of orbital tissues and is characteristic of Graves’ disease.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 38) Pretibial myxedema is classically seen in:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Pretibial myxedema is an autoimmune manifestation of Graves’ disease, although it is much less common than ophthalmopathy.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 39) The definitive treatment for toxic multinodular goitre in a fit patient is:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Surgery provides definitive treatment, especially for large goitres, compressive symptoms or suspected malignancy.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 40) Which nerve supplies the cricothyroid muscle?
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.option2: External branch of the superior laryngeal nerve
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Injury to this nerve affects pitch and voice projection, particularly in professional voice users.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 41) Which of the following is the most common cause of euthyroid goitre ?
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Iodine deficiency is the commonest cause of simple (euthyroid) goitre worldwide due to compensatory thyroid enlargement.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 42) A patient develops tingling around the mouth and carpopedal spasm after thyroidectomy. The most likely diagnosis is:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Post-thyroidectomy hypocalcaemia usually results from temporary hypoparathyroidism. Serum calcium should be checked immediately.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 43) The first-line treatment for hypothyroidism is:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Levothyroxine is the standard replacement therapy. The dose is adjusted according to serum TSH levels.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 44) Which drug is commonly used as the initial antithyroid medication in Graves’ disease?
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Carbimazole inhibits thyroid hormone synthesis and is the most commonly used antithyroid drug.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 45) Which drug rapidly controls adrenergic symptoms in thyrotoxicosis?
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Propranolol relieves tremor, tachycardia and palpitations. It does not reduce thyroid hormone production.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 46) The most life-threatening complication of untreated hyperthyroidism is:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Thyroid storm is an endocrine emergency characterized by severe thyrotoxicosis, hyperthermia and cardiovascular instability.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 47) Which investigation is most useful for confirming thyrotoxicosis?
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Suppressed TSH with elevated free T4 confirms primary hyperthyroidism.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 48) Which thyroid carcinoma is most commonly associated with cervical lymph node metastasis?
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Papillary carcinoma commonly spreads to regional cervical lymph nodes but still has an excellent prognosis.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 49) Which thyroid carcinoma commonly metastasizes to bone?
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Follicular carcinoma spreads hematogenously, with bone and lung being common metastatic sites.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 50) Which thyroid malignancy commonly presents in elderly patients with a rapidly enlarging neck mass?
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Rapid enlargement, compressive symptoms and poor prognosis are characteristic of anaplastic thyroid carcinoma.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 51) The commonest benign breast tumor in young women is:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Fibroadenoma is the commonest benign breast tumor, typically occurring in women below 30 years of age.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 52) Fibroadenoma is most commonly seen in women aged:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Fibroadenoma is most frequent during the reproductive years and is hormone-sensitive.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 53) The classical clinical feature of fibroadenoma is:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Fibroadenoma is often called the “breast mouse” because of its smooth, freely mobile nature.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 54) The commonest site of carcinoma of the breast is:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: The upper outer quadrant contains the greatest volume of breast tissue and is the most frequent site of breast cancer.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 55) The most common histological type of breast cancer is:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Invasive ductal carcinoma accounts for approximately 70–80% of breast malignancies.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 56) The most common presenting symptom of breast carcinoma is:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: A painless breast lump is the commonest presentation. Pain is usually a late or unrelated symptom.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 57) Skin dimpling in breast carcinoma is caused by involvement of:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Tumor infiltration shortens Cooper’s ligaments, producing skin dimpling or tethering.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 58) Peau d’orange appearance results from:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Obstruction of dermal lymphatics causes skin edema around hair follicles, producing the classic orange-peel appearance.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 59) The most common site of distant metastasis from breast carcinoma is:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Bone is the commonest site of distant spread, particularly the vertebrae, ribs and pelvis.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 60) The investigation of choice for diagnosing a palpable breast lump is:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Triple assessment includes clinical examination, imaging (USG/mammography) and FNAC/core biopsy, providing the highest diagnostic accuracy.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 61) The investigation of choice for screening breast cancer is:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Mammography is the standard screening test for breast cancer, especially in women over 40 years.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 62) The investigation of choice for a palpable breast lump in a woman aged 25 years is:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Breast ultrasound is preferred in younger women because dense breast tissue reduces mammographic sensitivity.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 63) The most accurate preoperative investigation for breast carcinoma is:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Core biopsy provides tissue architecture, allowing definitive histological diagnosis and receptor analysis.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 64) Which receptor status predicts response to trastuzumab?
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: HER2 overexpression predicts benefit from trastuzumab, which improves survival in HER2-positive breast cancer.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 65) Tamoxifen is primarily indicated in:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Tamoxifen is a selective estrogen receptor modulator used in hormone receptor-positive breast cancer.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 66) The commonest site of lymphatic spread from breast carcinoma is:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Axillary nodes are the first and most common site of regional lymphatic spread.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 67) The first draining lymph node from a breast carcinoma is called the:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: The sentinel node is the first lymph node receiving drainage from the tumor and is important for staging.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 68) Sentinel lymph node biopsy is mainly performed to:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: A negative sentinel node often avoids unnecessary axillary lymph node dissection.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 69) Which breast malignancy commonly presents with eczema-like changes of the nipple?
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Paget disease presents with chronic eczematous nipple changes and is usually associated with underlying ductal carcinoma.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 70) Bloody nipple discharge is most commonly caused by:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Intraductal papilloma is the commonest cause of spontaneous bloody nipple discharge.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 71) Which breast lesion has the highest risk of local recurrence?
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Phyllodes tumors may recur locally if excision margins are inadequate. Wide local excision is recommended.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 72) The treatment of choice for fibroadenoma larger than 3 cm is:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Large, enlarging or symptomatic fibroadenomas are usually managed by surgical excision.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 73) The commonest organism causing lactational breast abscess is:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Staphylococcus aureus is the predominant pathogen in lactational mastitis and breast abscess.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 74) The treatment of a breast abscess is:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Established breast abscesses require drainage in addition to appropriate antibiotic therapy.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 75) The most common benign breast condition is:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Fibrocystic change is the commonest benign breast disorder and often presents with cyclical breast pain.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 76) Cyclical mastalgia is most commonly associated with:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Breast pain that varies with the menstrual cycle is characteristic of fibrocystic breast changes.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 77) Which breast carcinoma has the best prognosis?
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Tubular carcinoma is a well-differentiated subtype with a favorable prognosis and low metastatic potential.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 78) Which breast carcinoma has the worst prognosis?
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Inflammatory carcinoma is highly aggressive, presenting with diffuse erythema, edema and dermal lymphatic invasion.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 79) A breast lump that increases rapidly in size during pregnancy is most likely:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Fibroadenomas are hormone-sensitive and may enlarge during pregnancy due to estrogen stimulation.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 80) The standard surgery for early breast cancer suitable for breast conservation is:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.option2: Wide local excision with sentinel lymph node biopsy
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Breast-conserving surgery followed by radiotherapy provides survival comparable to mastectomy in appropriately selected patients.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 81) The commonest benign tumor of the salivary gland is:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Pleomorphic adenoma (benign mixed tumor) is the commonest benign salivary gland neoplasm, most frequently involving the parotid gland.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 82) The salivary gland most commonly affected by tumors is:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: About 80% of salivary gland tumors arise in the parotid gland, and most are benign.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 83) The most common malignant salivary gland tumor is:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Mucoepidermoid carcinoma is the commonest malignant salivary gland neoplasm.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 84) Facial nerve palsy in a parotid swelling suggests:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Facial nerve involvement is highly suggestive of malignant parotid disease until proven otherwise.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 85) The investigation of choice for a parotid mass is:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: FNAC is the preferred initial investigation for evaluating salivary gland tumors.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 86) The commonest site of salivary calculi is:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: The long tortuous duct and viscous saliva predispose the submandibular gland to stone formation.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 87) A patient has painful swelling below the mandible during meals. The most likely diagnosis is:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Pain and swelling that worsen during meals are characteristic of salivary duct obstruction by a stone.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 88) The duct of the submandibular gland is:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Wharton duct drains the submandibular gland and opens beside the lingual frenulum.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 89) The duct of the parotid gland is:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Stensen duct crosses the masseter and opens opposite the upper second molar tooth.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 90) Which salivary gland has the highest proportion of malignant tumors?
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Although rare, tumors of the sublingual gland are malignant in the majority of cases.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 91) The treatment of pleomorphic adenoma of the parotid is:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.option3: Superficial parotidectomy with facial nerve preservation
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Enucleation has a high recurrence rate due to microscopic pseudopodia extending beyond the capsule.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 92) The most important nerve related to parotid surgery is:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: The facial nerve traverses the parotid gland and must be identified and preserved during surgery.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 93) The most common cause of acute bacterial sialadenitis is:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Staphylococcus aureus is the commonest organism causing acute suppurative sialadenitis.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 94) Which virus classically causes epidemic parotitis?
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Mumps is a viral infection causing painful bilateral parotid swelling.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 95) Adenoid cystic carcinoma is characterized by:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Adenoid cystic carcinoma is notorious for perineural spread and late local recurrence.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 96) Frey syndrome following parotidectomy is characterized by:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Aberrant regeneration of parasympathetic fibers causes sweating and flushing over the parotid region during eating.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 97) The most common complication after parotidectomy is:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Temporary facial nerve paresis is the commonest postoperative complication.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 98) Which salivary gland secretes predominantly serous saliva?
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: The parotid gland is almost entirely serous, whereas the sublingual gland is predominantly mucous.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 99) Which salivary gland secretes predominantly mucous saliva?
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: The sublingual gland is mainly mucous, while the submandibular gland produces mixed saliva.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 100) A painless, slowly enlarging parotid swelling present for years is most suggestive of:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Pleomorphic adenoma typically presents as a slow-growing, painless parotid mass.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 101) Which salivary gland tumor is strongly associated with cigarette smoking?
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Warthin tumor has a strong association with smoking and commonly occurs in older men.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 102) Warthin tumor most commonly arises in the:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Almost all Warthin tumors occur within the parotid gland, often in its tail.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 103) Which clinical feature favors a malignant salivary gland tumor?
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Facial nerve paralysis is a classic indicator of parotid malignancy.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 104) The preferred treatment for localized malignant parotid tumors is:
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.option1: Surgical excision with appropriate neck management
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Surgery is the primary treatment, with neck dissection and postoperative radiotherapy when indicated.

Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.question: 105) Which statement regarding salivary gland tumors is correct ?
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.option1: Warthin tumor commonly involves the submandibular gland.
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.option2: Most sublingual gland tumors are benign.
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.option3: Pleomorphic adenoma has malignant transformation potential if left untreated.
Thyroid, Breast & Salivary Gland.exp: Long-standing pleomorphic adenoma may undergo malignant transformation (carcinoma ex pleomorphic adenoma). Most parotid tumors are benign, whereas most sublingual tumors are malignant.
